subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
title: Listening and Speaking: Pronunciation and Vocabulary
overview: In this sub-strand you will say the sounds /ɪ/, /iː/, /s/, /ʃ/ and /əʊ/ clearly using words about hygiene and sanitation. You will also learn how to listen actively to a speaker, how to interrupt politely, and why we take turns when we talk in interviews and debates.

lessons.title: Sounds /ɪ/, /iː/, /s/, /ʃ/ and /əʊ/ in hygiene words
objectives: Say words with the sounds /ɪ/, /iː/, /s/, /ʃ/ and /əʊ/ correctly.
Tell the difference between pairs such as ship and sheep, sip and ship.
Use hygiene and sanitation words in sentences.
lessons.intro: Say these two words aloud: ship and sheep. They look almost the same, but one is a boat and the other is an animal. If you say the vowel wrongly, your listener hears a different word. Today we practise sounds that change meaning.
lessons.notes:
### The short sound /ɪ/ and the long sound /iː/
The sound /ɪ/ is short. Your mouth is relaxed and the sound is quick. Words: sit, bin, sink, dish, rinse, lid, fill.

The sound /iː/ is long. Stretch your lips a little, as if smiling, and hold the sound longer. Words: clean, sweep, feet, teeth, meal, sea, disease (the second part).

These pairs differ only in the vowel sound:

- ship – sheep
- sit – seat
- bin – bean
- fill – feel
- live – leave

### The sounds /s/ and /ʃ/
For /s/, keep your teeth close together and let air hiss out like a snake: soap, safe, sweep, dust, rinse.

For /ʃ/, push your lips forward and round them a little, like when you tell someone to be quiet: shh. Words: wash, flush, brush, shower, sanitation, infection. Notice that in sanitation and infection the letters ti make the /ʃ/ sound.

Pairs: sip – ship, sell – shell, sea – she, save – shave, sore – shore.

### The sound /əʊ/
This sound glides from one vowel to another. Start with your mouth open in the middle and finish with rounded lips: soap, home, toe, bowl, cold, clothes, no.

### Hygiene and sanitation words
Hygiene means keeping your body and things around you clean so that you stay healthy. Sanitation means the safe removal of waste such as faeces and refuse, for example by using a clean toilet or latrine. Other words you will use: flush, wipe, scrub, rinse, mop, broom, drainage, infection, diarrhoea, cholera.

- After using the toilet, flush it and wash your hands with soap.
- Dirty water can carry diseases such as cholera and diarrhoea.
- We sweep the classroom with a broom and mop the floor.

keyWords.meaning: keeping yourself and your surroundings clean to stay healthy
safe ways of getting rid of human waste and rubbish
wash something in clean water to remove soap or dirt
an illness caused when germs get into the body

examples.problem: Which word has the long sound /iː/: sit or seat?
Which word has the sound /ʃ/: sell or shell?
Pick the word with the sound /əʊ/: mop, soap, cup.

activity.title: Say it and riddle it
materials: Word cards: ship, sheep, sip, soap, sweep, wash, bin, bean, flush, home
steps: Listen to your teacher or an audio recording say each word, then repeat it after them.
In pairs, one learner says a word from a pair such as sit or seat; the partner points to the card they hear.
In groups, tell riddles that use the sounds, for example: I am white and slippery, and I get smaller every time you wash your hands. What am I? (soap)
Make one riddle of your own using a word with /ʃ/ or /əʊ/ and tell it to the class.

practice.question: Sort these words into /ɪ/ and /iː/: bin, clean, dish, sweep, sink, teeth.
practice.answer: /ɪ/: bin, dish, sink. /iː/: clean, sweep, teeth.

practice.question: Underline the letters that make the /ʃ/ sound in: wash, sanitation, brush.
Write two words with the sound /əʊ/ that are about cleanliness.
practice.answer: Any two, for example soap, clothes, bowl.

practice.question: Use the word flush in a sentence.
practice.answer: Example: Always flush the toilet after using it.

summary: /s/ hisses (sip); /ʃ/ is made with rounded lips (ship).
/əʊ/ glides, as in soap and home.
Hygiene and sanitation words help us talk about staying clean and healthy.

lessons.title: Active listening, polite interrupting and turn taking
objectives: Show a speaker that you are listening using words and body language.
Take turns in an interview or debate about hygiene.
lessons.intro: Imagine your class is holding a debate on whether every learner should carry a handkerchief to school. If everyone speaks at the same time, nobody hears anything. Good listeners and speakers follow simple rules.
lessons.notes:
### Listening actively
When someone gives a speech, tells a story or makes a presentation, show that you are following:

- Look at the speaker.
- Nod or smile when you agree or understand.
- Keep your hands and feet still; do not play with things.
- Ask a question or make a short comment when the speaker invites you.

These are verbal cues (words, such as "Yes, I see") and non-verbal cues (actions, such as nodding). They tell the speaker that you care about what they say.

When you are the speaker, engage your audience. Look at them, speak loudly enough, ask them a question, or let them guess the answer to a riddle.

### Interrupting politely
Sometimes you need to speak while someone is still talking, perhaps to ask for something to be repeated. Wait for a short pause, raise your hand if you are in class, then use polite words:

- Excuse me, may I say something?
- Sorry to interrupt, but could you repeat that?
- May I add something, please?

After you speak, say "Thank you. Please go on." Do not shout over the speaker or finish their sentences for them.

### Taking turns
In an interview, the interviewer asks one question and waits for the full answer before asking the next. In a debate, each speaker is given time and the others listen. Taking turns is important because:

- everyone gets a chance to share ideas;
- we hear every point clearly;
- it shows respect for others.

Here is part of an interview:

Amina: Excuse me, Otieno. May I ask you some questions about keeping clean?
Otieno: Yes, of course.
Amina: When do you wash your hands?
Otieno: I wash them before I eat and after I use the latrine.
Amina: Thank you. Why is that important?
Otieno: Because germs on dirty hands can cause diarrhoea.

keyWords.meaning: start speaking while another person is talking
a message sent without words, such as a nod or a smile
speaking one at a time and letting others finish
a formal discussion where people give different views on a topic

examples.problem: Your friend is telling a story and you did not hear a word. What do you say?
examples.answer: Sorry to interrupt, but could you repeat that word, please?

examples.problem: Name one non-verbal way to show you are listening.
examples.answer: Nodding, looking at the speaker, or smiling.

activity.title: Hygiene interviews
materials: A phone or tablet for recording (if available)
steps: In pairs, write three questions to ask about hygiene, for example: How do you keep your classroom clean?
Take turns to interview each other. The interviewer waits for each full answer.
Once during the interview, the listener interrupts politely to ask for something to be repeated.
Listen to a short poem or song about cleanliness read by the teacher and answer questions orally.
If a device is available, record your group reciting a short poem about hygiene.

practice.question: Write two polite phrases you can use to interrupt a speaker.
practice.answer: For example: Excuse me, may I say something? Sorry to interrupt, but may I ask a question?

practice.question: Give two reasons why we take turns in a debate.
practice.answer: Everyone gets a chance to speak, and we hear every point clearly (it also shows respect).

practice.question: Complete the sentence: A good listener looks at the speaker and ______.
practice.answer: nods / keeps quiet / asks questions when invited

summary: Show active listening with eye contact, nodding and short comments.
Interrupt only at a pause, using polite words such as Excuse me.
Take turns so that every speaker is heard.

quiz.question: Which word has the short sound /ɪ/?
quiz.explanation: Ship has the short /ɪ/; the others have the long /iː/.

quiz.question: Which pair differs only in the sounds /s/ and /ʃ/?
quiz.explanation: Sea begins with /s/ and she begins with /ʃ/.

quiz.question: Which letters make the /ʃ/ sound in the word sanitation?
quiz.explanation: In words ending in -tion, ti sounds /ʃ/.

quiz.question: Which of these shows you are listening actively?
quiz.explanation: Nodding is a non-verbal cue that shows you are following.

quiz.question: What is the most polite way to interrupt?
options: Excuse me, may I say something?
quiz.explanation: Excuse me and may I are polite words.

quiz.question: When is the best time to interrupt a speaker?
options: In the middle of a word
quiz.explanation: Waiting for a pause is polite.

quiz.question: Complete: After using the toilet, ______ it and wash your hands with soap.
quiz.explanation: We flush a toilet to remove the waste.

quiz.question: Which word means keeping yourself and your surroundings clean to stay healthy?
quiz.explanation: Hygiene is about cleanliness for good health.

quiz.question: Why do we take turns in an interview?
quiz.answer: So that each person can finish speaking and be heard clearly, which shows respect.
quiz.explanation: Turn taking lets every speaker be heard.
